truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.body_append:
## The 'half an hour ago I heard him call you a pedophile' set-up

On Covert Strategies Revealed in May 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) returned to the [Truck-and-Cat-in-the-Hat](/wiki/truck-and-cat-in-the-hat) episode with additional detail. He had been called down to the lieutenant's office earlier that day — usually a sign either of solitary or of being pressed to inform — because Jake Tapper had driven up from CNN to interview him and he had to sign a waiver. Cat in the Hat, standing two feet in front of him in the day room and not realising Kiriakou was behind him, told the man next to him: *"Did you hear Kiriakou got called down to the lieutenant's office? That guy's a rat. He got called down to rat us out."* Truck — the serial killer sitting next to Kiriakou watching a Steelers game — heard it and said *"did you hear that guy? He just said you're a rat."* Kiriakou, using what he calls his [CIA training](/wiki/kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics), answered: *"half an hour ago I heard him call you a pedophile."* Truck, without saying a word, got up and beat Cat in the Hat *"almost to death."* A helicopter landed in the yard to life-flight him to Pittsburgh; Truck was given five more years and sent to a medium-security prison. Cat in the Hat returned six weeks later, unable to meet Kiriakou's eye, and apologised: *"I should never have said that, it wasn't true."* Kiriakou answered: *"As God is my witness, if I ever hear my name cross your lips ever again, you're dead. And you'll never see it coming."*<Cite t="15:05" /><Cite t="15:36" /><Cite t="16:09" /><Cite t="16:41" />

john-kiriakou.body_append:
## The Lanzalotti pre-position

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said on Covert Strategies Revealed in May 2026 that he owes much of the safety of his prison term to an Italian inmate at [FCI Loretto](/wiki/fci-loretto) named Mark Lanzalotti — since become *"one of my best friends in life."* Lanzalotti read in the *New York Times* on the Sunday that Kiriakou was arriving at Loretto on the Thursday. Of his own initiative, Kiriakou says, Lanzalotti went to every Italian in the prison — *"Italians named Gambino, Genovese, Lucchese, you get the idea"* — and briefed them: *"There's a CIA guy coming here on Thursday. He's CIA, not FBI. FBI is rats and cops. The CIA protected us from the Muslims."* Kiriakou says the Italians *"welcomed me with open arms."*<Cite t="09:53" /><Cite t="10:23" />

## Farrakhan, the Aryans, and the Buracho

Simultaneously, and by mechanisms Kiriakou says he never understood, a rumour circulated among the Aryan prisoners that he had been an assassin for the [CIA](/wiki/cia) who had *"gone around the world killing Muslims"* after 9/11 — a legend the Aryans, in Kiriakou's telling, *"thought was fantastic"* and which secured him with them. On the same day Kiriakou arrived, the Nation of Islam newspaper carried a statement from [Louis Farrakhan](/wiki/louis-farrakhan) calling him *"a hero of the Muslim people"* for having *"stood up for Muslim human rights."* That covered the Muslim side.<Cite t="10:23" /><Cite t="10:55" /> The final flank Kiriakou attended to himself: assigned to a four-man cell crammed with six, four of the six were members of the Buracho, Norteño, Mexican Mafia and Jalisco Cartel factions. When the Buracho asked if he was educated and could write his appeal, Kiriakou did so pro bono. The appeal was denied, but the Buracho put the word out among the Mexicans that Kiriakou was *"a good guy … honest."* Kiriakou says the only trouble he had in prison thereafter was with *"the crooked, illiterate, corrupt guards."*<Cite t="10:55" /><Cite t="11:27" /><Cite t="11:59" />

## The FCI Loretto FOIA on himself

While still incarcerated, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) filed a Freedom of Information Act request on his own prison file. Most of the 250 pages he received back were routine, but half a dozen pages carried a *"FOIA exempt, do not release to inmate"* stamp and had been released regardless — *"either somebody was so stupid that they couldn't read at the Bureau of Prisons FOIA office, or they took pity on me."* One document was a memo from the [FCI Loretto](/wiki/fci-loretto) warden to all staff, dated the week before Kiriakou arrived, warning in block letters: *"CAUTION — INMATE HAS ACCESS TO THE MEDIA."* The same memo, Kiriakou says, justified holding him in a low-security facility rather than the minimum-security camp the sentencing judge had ordered on the grounds that he was *"trained in escape techniques"* — a claim Kiriakou answered with *"first of all, you watch too many movies — there is no training in escape techniques."*<Cite t="18:45" /><Cite t="20:18" /><Cite t="20:49" /><Cite t="21:20" />
